title: Market Metro — Agentic Commerce That Learns

style.captions: Readable DM Sans subtitles, short phrases, no additional footer commentary
style.motion: Clean white canvas, actual 3D metro grass and trees, native pedestrian animation, expressive stationary narrator character, and kinetic WHO/WHAT cards.

production.stage: White-canvas merchant story with landscaped native metro opener, recorded native pedestrians, new logo and enhanced sound; final MP4 not exported
production.capture: 13 source clips, including a presentation-only landscaped metro and native day-35 pedestrians. The traffic shot uses 16 representative shoppers plus the featured shopper to avoid visual crowding; underlying economic records are unchanged.
production.audio: Local Kokoro-82M neural female voice (af_heart), optimistic and warm; no hosted speech API
production.music: Original 120 BPM upbeat electronic groove with bass, percussion and plucks; ducked under narration. Audible purchase, notification and transition cues.
production.story: An ordinary morning for Leo: he opens, people walk past, days pass, and clues remain disconnected. WHO and WHAT are the story pivot into the agent.
production.reference: Original animated-infographic treatment: recurring characters, visual cause and effect, continuous narration. APAC footage remains read-only inspiration.
production.soundDesign: Original music plus 21 event cues: morning birds, shop bell, footsteps, page turns, thought-card pops and existing payment cues; shared master gain prevents clipping.
production.claimBoundary: Ontology training safeguards are shown as implemented capabilities; primary campaign gains are not attributed solely to ontology.
production.captions: Burned-in subtitles restored; synchronized WebVTT is also available.
production.character: Leo is an illustrative merchant persona for the narrative, not an identity in the payment record. The financial results remain controlled benchmark results.
production.question: Separate slower question take, 0.6-second pause, local Praat PSOLA rising final word; unchanged duration
production.branding: Redesigned route-M mark with a warm signal dot; shared by the app and video. Wordmark badge at upper left.

scenes.title: A normal day for Leo
scenes.captureAction: Show real 3D grass and trees around the metro, cut into recorded native shopper movement near the store, and bring Leo forward for the WHO/WHAT decision moment. No custom 2D walking cycle or colored street backdrop.
scenes.narration: It was a normal day for Leo. He opened his furniture shop, straightened the display, and waited. People hurried past. One checked their phone. Another glanced at the window and kept walking. Days went by, but the shop stayed quiet. Leo had data everywhere, yet he still couldn't tell who to reach or what to offer.

scenes.title: The question, then Market Metro
scenes.captureAction: Carry the white composition and Leo into the question, then reveal the new logo and ontology map with a clean transition.
scenes.narration: Could AI do this for Leo? Meet Market Metro. Its ontology connects shoppers, products and payments into one shared map, giving the agent meaningful evidence to work with.
onScreen: Could AI do this for Leo?

scenes.title: The right data for the question
scenes.captureAction: The ontology routes recommendation and inquiry history separately, while distinguishing input features from later outcome labels.
scenes.narration: The ontology maps each business question to the right training examples. Product recommendations and general inquiries follow separate paths, while later payment outcomes supply labels, not predictors.

scenes.title: From understanding to action
scenes.captureAction: Recurring illustrated characters and connected actions, with saved app recordings for technical and payment evidence.
scenes.narration: Now follow one saved reactivation campaign. The agent analyzes demand, chooses twenty eight days of history, and fits two models. A verifier tests the campaign before it reaches shoppers.

scenes.title: Test before sending
scenes.captureAction: Recurring illustrated characters and connected actions, with saved app recordings for technical and payment evidence.
scenes.narration: The first idea doesn't get a free pass. A verifier tests both rankings in separate development markets and selects the one that earns more while protecting merchants.

scenes.title: The recommendation becomes a purchase
scenes.captureAction: Recurring illustrated characters and connected actions, with saved app recordings for technical and payment evidence.
scenes.narration: On day thirty five, the selected recommendation reaches our shopper. They buy a ninety six dollar side table, and it arrives the next day; fixed rules left that same request unfilled.

scenes.title: A payment you can trace
scenes.captureAction: Recurring illustrated characters and connected actions, with saved app recordings for technical and payment evidence.
scenes.narration: We mirror that order once through PayPal Sandbox. The completed capture records the fee and merchant proceeds, then returns a receipt that links all the way back to the purchase.

scenes.title: What changed
scenes.captureAction: Show fixed 627 vs agent 643, sixteen highlighted payment icons, and incremental payment volume, merchant contribution and modeled PayPal net.
scenes.narration: Against fixed rules, sixteen more purchases were completed and kept. That's two thousand three hundred forty-five dollars in extra payment volume, over a thousand dollars in merchant contribution, and a hundred fifteen dollars in modeled PayPal net after AI cost.

scenes.title: Follow the full trail
scenes.captureAction: Recurring illustrated characters and connected actions, with saved app recordings for technical and payment evidence.
scenes.narration: Judges can follow the whole trail in AG Grid, from model training and the agent's decision to the PayPal receipt, instead of taking the result on trust.

uploadDraft.title: Market Metro | Agentic Commerce That Learns | PayPal AI Hackathon
uploadDraft.description:
Market Metro turns observed merchant activity into trained models, tested campaigns and traceable PayPal payments. This demo follows one saved 12-store, 600-shopper simulation from Day 1 to a recorded agent decision, purchase and native PayPal Sandbox receipt.

Against fixed rules in that same simulation: 16 more retained purchases, $1,024.86 additional merchant contribution, and $114.96 higher modeled PayPal net after estimated model cost. Merchant contribution includes inventory value. These are simulated outcomes, not actual PayPal profit. The $96 Sandbox capture is an existing order and uses fictitious funds.

Built with PayPal Sandbox, Gemini on Vertex AI, local scikit-learn models, SQLite, Three.js and AG Studio with native AG Grid, AG Charts and a custom PayPal evidence widget. The ontology feed comparison is a separate synthetic-data test.

Source and setup: https://github.com/VinceVence/market-metro
Original code: MIT. Third-party components retain their own licenses.
